spec: The seam, alone (THIN-SLICE-IMPLEMENTATION.md §4, §5 M0). src/engine.ts is the one door to the engine (§4.5). src/core/seam.ts: EngagementSpec (a campaign-free fielding: heroes, enemies, mapId, hexes, seed) -> battleOptionsOf(spec): BattleOptions (the joint §4.1 names, kept campaign-free until M1 gives makeBattleState a campaign) -> createBattle -> runBattle -> makeBattleResult(events): EngagementResult, an events-to-result FOLD (§4.2) that never reaches into Ctx: outcome, turns, enemy phases, and per-unit rows keyed to the spec's roster by index (uid 100+i) carrying downed, dead, damageTaken, kills. runEngagement(spec) is the three in a row. No campaign code.
expect: ISC-002: running a known fielding yields per-hero rows whose downed/dead/damageTaken/kills equal what a hand count of the same event log gives, and a wiped fielding reports every hero downed or dead. ISC-003: the only file importing an engine path is src/engine.ts, and the events the fold read begin with battle.begin and end with battle.end emitted by the engine's own runBattle.

spec: CampaignState as plain data (Law 5b; GAME-ARCHITECTURE.md §1): week, cursor, purse (Record<CurrencyId, number>), renown, roster, assignments, territories, buildings, revealed, unlocks, threat, cups — plus the rows SKELETON-SETTLED.md:57-61 flags as owed: losses, quests in flight, captured; corruption stored. makeCampaign(seed, legacy, options). One mutator module and one emit; every state change goes through it (Law 3). The item also ships a loadable fixture — fixtures/slice-prep.json — a Campaign positioned at Combat Prep (cursor.step reveal) with a small roster and an engagement.conquer on a Territory row, so the next items have something to load (ruling 2026-09-01: load state → decide what happened → exit).
expect: ISC-004: JSON.stringify/parse round-trips a fresh Campaign and a Campaign mid-Week to deep-equal values; no field holds a class, Map, Set or function.

spec: Combat Prep as cursor transitions (GAME-ARCHITECTURE.md §4 Inside Combat Prep; SKELETON-SETTLED.md:127): reveal → council → deploy → equip, then battle. viewCombatPrep(campaign, engagement) lists the enemies and the condition at reveal; listCouncilOptions offers exactly three placeholder tactic rows under the reserved test.* kind (ruling 2026-09-01 — until tactic.* is declared) and performing one records it; canDeploy/performDeploy/performUndeploy under the base size limit 4 (§2.3 axis 1); equip is a step that exists and passes through (nothing priced yet). The four steps are rows the machine reads in order, not four hardcoded cases.
expect: ISC-026: the cursor visits reveal, council, deploy, equip in that order. ISC-027: at reveal the view lists every enemy and no choice is recorded. ISC-028: three options, one taken, two gone. ISC-029: the fifth deploy is refused at limit 4.

spec: The battle screen and the outcome panel, in SLICE.html (self-contained, built by tools/build-slice.mjs with esbuild from engine/node_modules — ruling 2026-09-01). The board and every unit come from the engine's own setup (createBattle at t=0 through the seam; nothing runs). The panel sets everything a battle could decide as an EngagementResult — outcome, per unit lifeState/downed/dead/damage/kills, phases — and validateResult accepts a panel-built result and a fold-built result alike. resolveReckoning(campaign, engagement, result) proposes XP per unit and a wound per hero; every proposal is editable before apply.
expect: ISC-030 (H): the map with every deployed hero and every enemy, still. ISC-031: one result shape, one validator, applyBattleResult blind to the producer. ISC-032: proposals editable, written exactly.
note: ISC-031 and ISC-032 name the writer and land with reckoning.apply (2026-09-01); ISC-034 is the proposal half. SLICE.html stops at the tally until the writer lands.

spec: applyBattleResult(campaign, engagement, result) — the only writer (GAME-ARCHITECTURE.md §1 rule 2) — and the tail: wounds from downed/dead (a level on hero.wound; commitmentOf -> 'wounded' above the threshold), Renown +1 per Engagement won (KINGDOM-DESIGN.md §3A), the losses counter, Salvage only from a first Conquer (SKELETON-SETTLED.md:104,108), the reward draft 3-keep-1 (7-KINGDOM-SETTLED.md), the difficulty number Σ(hero levels, civilians ÷2 ⌊⌋) + 2×week − 5×losses + 3×corruption counting everyone alive (SKELETON-NOTES.md:675).
expect: ISC-014..020 as written in THIN-SLICE-IMPLEMENTATION.md §6 — the scan finds one writer; a lost battle wounds and pays no Salvage; Renown rises exactly 1 per win; re-conquest pays Renown and never Salvage; a wounded hero is refused deployment; the draft offers 3 and keeps 1; the difficulty number matches the hand sum on three authored rosters. ISC-033: after apply the cursor is past the battle, the save round-trips, a second apply is refused.
note: ISC-019 (the reward draft) moved to rewards.draft 2026-09-01 — it is the rewards screen, not the writer.

spec: The Week: six Stage rows in src/content (stage.buy, stage.quest, stage.defend, stage.conquer, stage.build, stage.mend — KINGDOM-DESIGN.md §3, GLOSSARY.md) read in registry order by a machine in src/core that knows no Stage by name. beginWeek/endWeek/tickWeek, beginStage/endStage, canAdvance/performAdvance, weekOf/stageOf/cursorOf (GAME-ARCHITECTURE.md §2.6). Every Stage emits stage.begun and stage.ended even when it resolves to nothing (§2.1). The cursor holds week, stage, step, engagement, and the battle's SEED AND OPTIONS — never its state (§4.4). The world screen in SLICE.html: the Week and Stage named, Next to pass through a Stage that resolves to nothing; the Conquer Stage picks up the fixture engagement until the map (M6) offers real ones.
expect: ISC-005: a Week visits the six ids in the ruled order, and disabling stage.mend (KINGDOM_DISABLE_IDS) makes the order test fail. ISC-006: stage.begun/stage.ended pairs appear for every Stage of an empty Week. ISC-007: at every cursor position, stringify/parse then advance gives the same event stream as advancing the original. tools/probe.mts lands with this item: it runs N Weeks and reports whether an id appears in the log.

spec: The slice map as content (GAME-ARCHITECTURE.md §2.4; THIN-SLICE-REVIEW.md §G2): four territory.<realm>.* rows — the Kingdom Territory plus three, the first conquest carrying a critical building — with adjacency and a map id each. canClaim/performClaim/performLose; the Kingdom Territory's row says it cannot be lost (SKELETON-SETTLED.md:80-81). stage.conquer produces an Engagement through the seam and a won one claims the Territory and any building on it (7-KINGDOM-SETTLED.md). The first vertical slice: Week -> Conquer -> battle -> result -> Week N+1. Plus the defend roll: stage.defend rolls once on cup.threat at 6% per owned Territory (THIN-SLICE-REVIEW.md §G2) and produces at most one engagement.defend on an owned non-kingdom Territory (or the Sanctuary, whose loss costs resources instead). The world screen shows the four, owned and not, and lets you pick a conquest.
expect: ISC-011: listTerritories returns four rows, one flagged kingdom, one carrying a building. ISC-012: a heroClear Conquer claims the Territory and its building; a wipe claims nothing. ISC-013: performLose on an owned non-kingdom Territory makes it conquerable again; on the Kingdom Territory it is refused and costs resources and wounds per its stakes row. ISC-035: over 200 Weeks with four owned the defend rate lands within 24% ± 6.
note: variants named from src/content/territories.ts, the realm manifest — the Ridge (GLOSSARY.md's example) and the Highlands (an engine map name).

spec: Assignments under amended Law 17 (SKELETON-SETTLED.md:102; GAME-ARCHITECTURE.md §2.3): campaign.assignments: Record<HeroId, {field?, city?}>; commitmentOf(campaign, heroId, slot) -> 'free' | 'onQuest' | 'committed' | 'wounded' | 'unavailable' | 'captured' | 'dead'; canCommit is the only legality check; a quest takes both slots; listAvailable(campaign, stageId) reads commitmentOf and nothing else has an opinion about availability.
expect: ISC-008: a second field or city commit in one Week is refused by canCommit. ISC-009: a hero on a quest is absent from listAvailable for every Stage. ISC-010: commitmentOf returns 'unavailable' for a hero the Week's roll kept home, and no other function in src/ inspects hero availability (a static scan).
note: variants: the two Stage rows that spend the two slots — listAvailable reads which slot from the row (spends: assignments → field, city-assignments → city), so the second slot is data.

spec: The purse (Law 18; 7-KINGDOM-SETTLED.md Currencies): four currency.* rows in src/content; balanceOf/canAfford/applySpend/applyGrant with a causeId on every grant (GAME-ARCHITECTURE.md §2.6). Payouts are DATA — a table of which Stage grants which currency — so 'Salvage only from Conquer' is a row the machine reads, and deleting that row is what turns ISC-022 red. stage.buy spends the purse and nothing else. Mend: the four labours as rows (no id kind yet — §9 blocker 9) with the settled yields — Farm 5+2×Fields Supplies, Pray 4+1×Abbeys Faith, Delve 4+1×Wellsprings Mana — each a city Assignment resolved at stage.mend; Heal and Rest yield nothing. Buy: performRecruit spends Faith and adds a hero from a small recruit pool (the Beacon, thin); performHeal spends Faith and lowers a wound one level.
expect: ISC-021: four ids exist and canAfford is false when the named currency is short whatever the others hold; disabling currency.salvage makes the test fail. ISC-022: across a simulated run every resource.gained event whose currency is Salvage has a Conquer Engagement as its cause. ISC-036: the yields to the number. ISC-037: recruit spends Faith, adds a row, refused when short. ISC-038: heal spends Faith, lowers one level, refused on a whole hero.

spec: The reward draft — 3 drawn, keep 1 (7-KINGDOM-SETTLED.md; keep-2 rejected). listRewardOffers draws three item rows on cup.reward keyed by the Engagement; performTakeReward keeps one into the stash and burns two; the rewards step sits between reckoning and open. Level-up: canLevelUp at 20 · 100 · 250 XP (GLOSSARY.md, soft), performLevelUp +1 level, no specialty pick yet; the levelUp step follows rewards.
expect: ISC-019: three offers, one kept, two gone, the same three on reload. ISC-039: level at the thresholds, refused below.
note: variants: two reward rows of different slots — a weapon and an armor — drawn by the same draft.

spec: The Forge as rows from the settled tree (7-KINGDOM-SETTLED.md: repair 10, then Blades · Bows · Shields · Light · Heavy as a fan, then the chain — 190 total; THE-KINGDOM.html for the nodes): building.forge with nodes, prices in Salvage, parents. stage.build: canBuild/costOfBuild/performBuild; a node needs its parents built and the purse. The shelf: with the repair node built, listShopItems offers the starting weapons and tier-1 armors (item rows the engine already fields); performBuyItem spends Supplies into the stash; the equip step gains performEquip onto a deployed hero.
expect: ISC-040: a node bought spends its price and is marked; unmet parents or purse refused. ISC-041: the shelf sells for Supplies and the item equips at the equip step.
note: building.chapel as the second instance: its root node only, to prove the tree machine is data — the full Chapel is out of the slice.

spec: A new Campaign from nothing (GAME-ARCHITECTURE.md §2.5): makeCampaign(seed) at Week 0 with an empty roster; listDraftOffers shows three hero rows stat-less (name, class, personality, prose — SKELETON-SETTLED.md:124); performDraft puts one on the roster. The five prologue battles as Engagement rows from ENEMY-REVIEW.md Battles 1–5 with their civilians; the cadence 1 · +2 · +1 per battle to six drafted heroes; the Kingdom Territory is taken on the last; a loss before that ends the Campaign (performEndCampaign, then a fresh makeCampaign).
note: variants: the prologue battles are engagement.conquer rows flagged prologue (no kind of their own — the open label question), and the ruled first draftee (engine/DECISIONS.md 2026-08-26) as a hero-pool row; both live in the autoplayed opening. Whether the prologue pays Renown is SWITCHES.md prologue.paysRenown.

spec: The Charter (KINGDOM-DESIGN.md §3A; SKELETON-SETTLED.md:106): Renown is the entire budget, one Renown one purchase, unlock.* rows in src/content; an Article slot opens at Renown 10 and every 5 after, 1-9 is the free spine. canPurchase/performPurchase; hasUnlock/listUnlocks.
expect: ISC-023: a purchase costs exactly one Renown and no currency can substitute. ISC-024: listArticleSlots is empty below 10, one at 10, two at 15, and a Provision is what 1-9 buys.
note: variants: two unlock.* rows named from KINGDOM-DESIGN.md §3A when worked (GLOSSARY.md example shape: unlock.field-size.5).

spec: The thin screens (THIN-SLICE-REVIEW.md §G2 list): screen.title and screen.mode-select as stubs in front of the Campaign (Start Game → new Campaign or the browser save; other modes locked); screen.roster (every hero, class, level, XP, wound, availability); the unavailability roll between Buy and Quest — a roll on cup.unavailability marking heroes unavailable for the Week with story lines (KINGDOM-DESIGN.md §3, numbers soft); one authored quest at stage.quest taking both slots for N Weeks and returning with tickWeek.
expect: ISC-046 (unavailability), ISC-047 (one quest), ISC-048/049/050 (H — world map, roster, title).

spec: tools/slice-run.mjs: from a new save, with no human input (an authored default choice at every decision), the run advances Week by Week until the first Article threshold fires (THIN-SLICE-REVIEW.md §G ruling 1). --until article-1 --assert no-out-systems proves the terminus depends on none of §8's systems. BLOCKED on §9 item 1 (the P11 encounter format; battleList.rows is empty) for the eleven battles it needs — until then it runs the authored five and stops, red.
expect: ISC-001: exit 0 with the Article threshold event in the log at battle 11. ISC-025: exit 0 with every §8 system absent or stubbed.
